title: Right derived functor on the unbounded derived category
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], and let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be additive [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Write $K(\mathcal C)$ for cochain complexes modulo chain homotopy and $Q_{\mathcal C}:K(\mathcal C)\to D(\mathcal C)$ for localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and similarly for $\mathcal D$. A complex $I$ is K-injective if every chain map from an acyclic complex to $I$ is homotopic to zero; assume every complex of $\mathcal C$ admits a quasi-isomorphism to a K-injective complex. Write $F_K:K(\mathcal C)\to K(\mathcal D)$ for degreewise application of $F$.

The right derived functor is the total right derived functor $RF:D(\mathcal C)\to D(\mathcal D)$ of $Q_{\mathcal D}\circ F_K$ with respect to quasi-isomorphisms, whose existence is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]. It has a unit $\eta:Q_{\mathcal D}\circ F_K\Rightarrow RF\circ Q_{\mathcal C}$: for every $G:D(\mathcal C)\to D(\mathcal D)$ the map $\operatorname{Nat}(RF,G)\to\operatorname{Nat}(Q_{\mathcal D}\circ F_K,G\circ Q_{\mathcal C})$, $\beta\mapsto(\beta Q_{\mathcal C})\circ\eta$, is bijective. This specifies the pair $(RF,\eta)$ up to unique isomorphism compatible with the unit. The component $\eta_I$ is an isomorphism for every K-injective $I$. For any K-injective resolution $s:K\to I$, there is the canonical isomorphism $RF(Q_{\mathcal C}K)\cong Q_{\mathcal D}(F_K I)$. This is the meaning of the notation $RF(K)=F(I)$.

proof.text: The homotopy categories $K(\mathcal C)$ and $K(\mathcal D)$ are triangulated with the stated cone triangles, and $Q_{\mathcal D}$ is exact, by [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated]. Degreewise application of $F$ defines $F_K$. The finite-biproduct condition in [def-sp-left-exact-additive] gives additivity on morphisms explicitly: $a+b=\nabla\circ(a\oplus b)\circ\Delta$, and the canonical biproduct identifications identify $F(\Delta)$ and $F(\nabla)$ with the diagonal and codiagonal. Thus $F(a+b)=F(a)+F(b)$; preservation of the zero object gives $F(0)=0$, and hence $F(-a)=-F(a)$. Indeed, $F(d^{n+1})F(d^n)=F(0)=0$, and applying $F$ to a chain homotopy equation $a-b=dh+hd$ gives $F(a)-F(b)=F(d)F(h)+F(h)F(d)$, since $F$ is additive [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Under the canonical biproduct identifications, applying $F$ to the cone differential $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}d_L&a\\0&-d_K\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ gives the cone differential for $F(a)$; it also respects the inclusion and minus-projection maps and the shifted differential $-d_K$. The degreewise identities $F(K[1])^n=F(K^{n+1})=(F_K K)[1]^n$ therefore give an isomorphism of complexes, natural because both sides send a map $a$ in degree $n$ to $F(a^{n+1})$. Thus $Q_{\mathcal D}\circ F_K$ sends each cone triangle to its image cone triangle. The cone description and localization in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and the definition of exact functor in [def-weil-triangulated-category] show that this is an exact functor from $K(\mathcal C)$ to the triangulated category $D(\mathcal D)$. No exactness of $F$ on the abelian categories is needed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] with $\mathcal A=\mathcal C$, $\mathcal T=D(\mathcal D)$ and its input functor equal to $Q_{\mathcal D}\circ F_K$. The K-injective resolution hypothesis is exactly the assumed existence of a quasi-isomorphism from every complex to a K-injective one; step 1 verifies exactness and the target triangulated structure. The cited statement gives a functor $RF$, a unit $\eta$, the bijection on natural transformations for every $G$, and invertibility of $\eta_I$ for every K-injective $I$. Choose such a universal pair as the definition. For any other universal pair the two bijections give comparison transformations preserving units; their composites preserve the respective units, so injectivity of the bijections makes the composites identities. Hence the chosen definition is unique up to the stated unique isomorphism.

proof.text: For a K-injective resolution $s:K\to I$, $Q_{\mathcal C}(s)$ is invertible by the localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Therefore so is $RF(Q_{\mathcal C}(s))$. Compose it with $\eta_I^{-1}$ to obtain $RF(Q_{\mathcal C}K)\xrightarrow{RF(Q_{\mathcal C}s)}RF(Q_{\mathcal C}I)\xrightarrow{\eta_I^{-1}}Q_{\mathcal D}(F_K I)$. This is the asserted isomorphism for every chosen resolution. Its compatibility with the unit is exactly the naturality equation $RF(Q_{\mathcal C}s)\circ\eta_K=\eta_I\circ Q_{\mathcal D}(F_K s)$. It requires neither that $s$ be degreewise monic nor that $F$ preserve quasi-isomorphisms. Writing this composite as $c_s$, cancellation of $\eta_I$ in that equation gives $c_s\circ\eta_K=Q_{\mathcal D}(F_Ks)$, explicitly the required compatibility.
